skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Review x402socks proxy packages, quote costs, and manage proxy tokens. Purchases use USDC on Base and require explicit approval.
skill.summary: Quote x402 proxy access and manage credentials for authorized HTTPS traffic.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most static flags match documentation, payment metadata, or expected helper operations. No evidence of credential stealing or embedded prompt injection was found. Key risks include incomplete destination checks, weak purchase reconciliation and approval binding, credential exposure in insecure modes, and untrusted provider output.

remediation.issue: Fetch examples do not enforce destination policy.
remediation.suggestion: Abort on failed URL validation. Enforce the allowlist outside the browser for every connection, and verify redirects and service worker traffic before enabling browser use.

remediation.issue: Payment checks can fail open and approvals are tied to paths.
remediation.suggestion: Stop on inconclusive validation and reconcile durable settlement state. Bind authorization to the actual signer and atomically claim a verified approval identifier before any signature.

remediation.issue: Payment examples trust a runtime-selected helper executable.
remediation.suggestion: Use a trusted absolute helper path with restricted permissions. Do not accept executable path overrides in the signer environment.

remediation.issue: Alternate origins and legacy modes can expose credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove insecure overrides from credential-bearing commands and legacy transport recipes. Require exact provider origins, including ports, and use only the TLS proxy.

remediation.issue: Credential examples bypass hardened storage checks.
remediation.suggestion: Reuse the helper's private file checks and token validation. Keep reusable tokens and live recovery proofs out of temporary files, logs, and command arguments.

remediation.issue: The egress test discloses the direct public IP.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent for the direct baseline or allow an approved IP comparison service controlled by the operator.

remediation.issue: Untrusted provider text can enter the agent transcript.
remediation.suggestion: Validate response lengths and types, remove raw provider keys from errors, and label remaining provider text as untrusted data before presenting it.

semantic_findings.title: Shell examples continue after target rejection
semantic_findings.description: Both curl examples run the target check and then invoke curl without requiring a successful check. A failed check does not stop an ordinary shell from making the request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Neither snippet enables fail-fast behavior or makes the curl invocation conditional on the preceding validator.

semantic_findings.title: Browser allowlist does not cover all traffic
semantic_findings.description: The Playwright recipe relies on context routing and a final URL check. Redirect chains and service worker requests are not fully controlled, so an unapproved connection can occur before rejection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recipe uses a default context and relies on a route handler that cannot enforce every redirected or service worker request.

semantic_findings.title: Purchase reconciliation can proceed after an inconclusive check
semantic_findings.description: Both payment examples continue when token validation fails for any reason. They do not check saved settlement state before progressing, so transient errors can lead to duplicate purchases.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The catch paths collapse helper and network errors into absence of a valid token. Neither example consults a settlement record before claiming approval.

semantic_findings.title: Purchase approval is not enforced as a trusted single-use decision
semantic_findings.description: The examples trust a local approval record and mark its pathname, not a unique approval. The main instructions also delay consumption until after signing, conflicting with the reference.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Exclusive creation prevents concurrent reuse of one pathname, but the examples do not authenticate the approval or bind it to a durable one-use identifier.

semantic_findings.title: Python preflight does not verify the actual signer
semantic_findings.description: The Python example compares an environment value against the approved address. It does not bind the signer that will authorize a real USDC payment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example is labeled preflight and contains no signer. A deployment must verify the actual signing account separately.

semantic_findings.title: Provider-controlled text can reach the agent
semantic_findings.description: Public responses, quote fields, and some error messages can expose arbitrary provider text to the agent. Printable ASCII and field allowlists do not make that text trustworthy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The public JSON path prints the parsed response, quote output includes free text, and token errors print provider-supplied keys. No embedded injection attempt was found.

content.user_title: Review and Manage Paid Proxy Access
content.value_statement: Teams testing authorized HTTPS services may need a regional exit and a clear spending decision. This skill provides package quotes, proxy health checks, and token management.
actual_capabilities: List provider health, catalog entries, and exits marked as available.
Read a live x402 quote and check that its amount fits an explicit USDC ceiling.
Document how to compare approved payment terms before a host-provided wallet signer authorizes a purchase.
Store, validate, rotate, or recover proxy tokens with the shell helper.
Compare direct and proxied egress IPs using an external IP check service.
limitations: A purchase requires an external signer and a wallet funded with USDC on Base. The shell helper does not sign payments.
Changing your network exit does not grant access to a destination or guarantee anonymity.
The example browser and shell clients do not reliably enforce destination restrictions. Use an independently controlled allowlist.
Live prices, exit availability, session limits, and quotas can change.

use_cases.title: Check regional exit availability
use_cases.description: Review provider health and available regional exits before planning a check of a service your team owns.

use_cases.title: Review a proposed purchase
use_cases.description: Compare the package quote, recipient, and exact USDC amount with the team's approved spending limit.

use_cases.title: Triage an existing proxy token
use_cases.description: Separate token problems from service outages and identify when recovery may be needed without buying another package.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize provider status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check service health and list the exits marked available. Do not read credentials, contact target sites, or purchase access.

prompt_templates.title: Review a package quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote my selected package within my stated USDC cap. Report the recipient, amount, and included limits. Do not sign or send payment.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an existing token
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate my existing token without revealing it. Summarize the result and stop before rotating, recovering, or purchasing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an authorized staging check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the proposed TLS proxy plan for our staging service. Identify which controls enforce allowed destinations and prevent duplicate charges. Do not run the plan.

output_examples.input: Check whether the proxy service has any available exits.
output_examples.output: The provider reports healthy service and two available exits in this example. No target requests or payments were made.

output_examples.input: Review a package against my one USDC limit.
output_examples.output: The quote is one USDC and meets your cap. Review the package and recipient before approving it. No payment was signed.

output_examples.input: My proxy stopped accepting requests. Is my token valid?
output_examples.output: Token validation was inconclusive because the service timed out. No token was revealed and no replacement was purchased.

best_practices: Require a fresh approval for the exact package, recipient, wallet, and amount before signing.
Keep tokens in private storage and use an independently enforced destination allowlist for authorized traffic.
Reconcile pending payments and existing tokens before considering a new purchase.
anti_patterns: Using a proxy to bypass access rules, blocks, or rate limits.
Sharing a private key, reusable token, or live recovery signature in chat or logs.
Signing again after a timeout or another payment challenge without reconciling the first authorization.

faq.question: Can I check prices without paying?
faq.answer: Yes. Catalog and quote requests do not sign a payment. A live quote needs a USDC cap.

faq.question: What do I need to buy a package?
faq.answer: You need explicit approval, a compatible wallet funded with USDC on Base, and a supported external signer.

faq.question: Does the helper use SOCKS5?
faq.answer: No. The helper uses TLS HTTP CONNECT. The provider's legacy options do not encrypt proxy credentials on the client-to-proxy hop.

faq.question: Does a proxy make traffic anonymous?
faq.answer: No. It changes the network exit but does not guarantee anonymity or grant permission to access a site.

faq.question: What should I do if payment settled but the token is missing?
faq.answer: Reconcile the settlement and review recovery with the paying wallet. Do not pay again just because the token is missing.

faq.question: Does testing egress reveal my direct IP?
faq.answer: Yes. The test compares a direct request and a proxied request to an external IP service.
